parts.label: (b)
(b)(i)
parts.text: State the direction of the magnetic field.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Show that the magnitude of the force exerted on each electron by the magnetic field is $1.3 \times 10^{-14}\text{ N}$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: On Fig. 6.1, draw an arrow to indicate the direction of the centripetal acceleration of the electron where it enters the magnetic field at point $X$.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Use the information in (b)(ii) to calculate the distance $d$ between the path of the electrons entering the magnetic field and the path of the electrons leaving it.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The electrons in (b) are replaced with positrons that are moving with speed $3.4 \times 10^7 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ along the same initial path as the electrons.
The positrons enter the magnetic field at point $X$ on Fig. 6.1.

On Fig. 6.1, draw a line to show the path of the positrons through the magnetic field.
